subject: Bifactor Model: Computation of robust CFI / RMSEA failed

messages.author: 1933d661a0a10f37
messages.subject: Bifactor Model: Computation of robust CFI / RMSEA failed
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am working on replicating a hierarchical factor structure of a model that consists of one general factor and five specific factors. The model was originally developed using a second-order factor structure, but I aim to model it as a bifactor model to allow for separate effects on both the general and specific factors. The scale includes 18 items, with each factor measured by 3 to 4 items. The sample size is N=1078, clustered across 13 schools.

Initially, I attempted to replicate the factor structure as proposed by the original authors. The overall model fit was acceptable (CFI = 0.947, TLI = 0.931, RMSEA = 0.051, SRMR = 0.051), but there were issues with the local fit for one specific factor measured by three items:

  • One item (Item 3) did not load significantly on the specific factor (p = 0.161).
  • Another item (Item 13) was marginally significant (p = 0.049).
  • The third item (Item 17) loaded significantly on the specific factor (p = 0.012), but its variance was not significantly different from zero (p = 0.111).
  • All three items loaded significantly on the general factor.


In response, I respecified the model by removing one specific factor and allowing Items 3, 13, and 17 to load only on the general factor. While all parameters were significant, the fit indices slightly declined: CFI = 0.940, TLI = 0.923, RMSEA = 0.053, and SRMR = 0.051.

To retain the five specific factors for subsequent analyses, I decided to remove Item 3 entirely and reran the model with five specific factors, leaving one specific factor measured by only two items. This model showed improved fit indices: CFI = 0.952, TLI = 0.936, RMSEA = 0.050, and SRMR = 0.047. Additionally, all parameters were significant.

However, I consistently receive the following warnings:

  1. lavaan->lav_fit_cfi_lavobject():
    Computation of robust CFI failed.
  2. lavaan->lav_fit_rmsea_lavobject():
    Computation of robust RMSEA failed.

I am concerned that these warnings may indicate issues with model identification and could cause problems with subsequent analysis.

Am I correct in my assessment, or could there be another issue at play?
Does anyone have experience with modeling specific factors measured by only 2 items in a bifactor model?

I need some help deciding between the three models.

Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 177d6b42224d530a
messages.subject: Re: Bifactor Model: Computation of robust CFI / RMSEA failed
parts:
Hi lavaanrookie99,

You mentioned that you specify "Items 3, 13, and 17 to load only on the general factor." 

In this case you have no longer a general factor. Your general factor become a reference domain defined by these three items.

On this topic see :

Eid, M., Geiser, C., Koch, T., & Heene, M. (2017). Anomalous results in g-factor models: Explanations and alternatives. Psychological Methods, 22(3), 541–562. https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000083

A recent research suggest that problems of non significant item loadings can be explained by the sum of squared factor loadings per domain factor that could be low in your case and not fixed specific factor (even if a bifactor model assume random items as well as random specific factors for proper definition).

 On this topic :

https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00273171.2023.2228757?scroll=top&needAccess=true

For problem of identification see :

Green, S. and Y. Yang (2018). Empirical underidentification with the bifactor model: A case

study. Educational and Psychological Measurement 78 (5), 717–736. 

and :

https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0013164417719947

I hope It will help you.

Best 

Pierre-Charles

messages.subject: Re: Bifactor Model: Computation of robust CFI / RMSEA failed
parts:
Dear Pierre-Charles,

Thank you so much for your literature recommendations! Unfortunately, I wasn't able to access the Petras paper.

The Eid paper was very helpful. The Bifactor S-1 model seems like a reasonable alternative, although I am unsure whether my hypotheses can still be addressed, as the interpretation changes and I can no longer make assumptions about a general factor.

I’m now considering removing Item 3 entirely. I could avoid underidentification by setting the factor loadings of the two remaining indicators equal. This approach results in an acceptable fit, but I’m uncertain about what this means for the interpretation of my CFA.

Am I correct in assuming that the domain-specific factor is not empirically supported, given the low factor loadings? Would it still be acceptable to retain the factor with two indicators, using constrained loadings, in my subsequent bifactor SEM, for theoretical reasons?

Or would you recommend keeping all indicators and simply being cautious when interpreting the results for that domain-specific factor?

I would be very grateful for your advice.

Greetings 
lavaanrookie99

messages.author: 177d6b42224d530a
messages.subject: Re: Bifactor Model: Computation of robust CFI / RMSEA failed
parts:
Hi lavaanrookie99,

With a bifactor S-1 model you can't ask the same question as with a bifactor symmetrical model. 

Also, Petras work shows that if it improves interpretability it does seem not avoid anomalies. 

You should not leave the entire set of items on this specific factor. 

Unfortunately I don't how exactly how to interpret the model with two items set to equality as I never had to face this problem.

Best

Pierre-Charles
